What is kitchen design?

Planning the room before building it.

Kitchen design is the practical and visual planning of the room. It starts with the sink, stove and refrigerator work triangle, then resolves the layout, modular or custom cabinetry, storage, countertops and appliance positions.

It also brings lighting, ventilation, materials and 3D visualization into one coordinated plan. Kitchen design sets the decisions. Renovation is the execution of those decisions on site.

CleanSink
CookStove
StoreRefrigerator

What's included

Every kitchen decision, coordinated.

Eight connected parts shape a kitchen that works well, looks considered and is ready to build.

Scroll the scope

01

Layout Planning & Work Triangle

L-shaped, U-shaped, galley, island and one-wall plans with clear sink, stove and refrigerator movement.

02

Modular Kitchen Design

Planned base, wall, tall and drawer units with reliable dimensions, hardware and installation logic.

03

Custom Kitchen Design

Bespoke joinery for irregular rooms, specific storage needs and a tailored architectural fit.

04

Smart Storage Design

Pull-outs, drawer systems, corner solutions, pantry storage and full-height utility units.

05

Countertops & Backsplash

Practical selections across marble, granite and quartz, coordinated with wall protection and detailing.

06

Appliance Integration

Positions and clearances for the chimney, hob, sink, dishwasher, oven and refrigerator.

07

Lighting & Ventilation Design

General, task and under-cabinet lighting with planned airflow and chimney extraction.

08

Materials & Finishes

Cabinet finishes including lamination, acrylic and PU, paired with suitable hardware and surfaces.

Kitchen layouts we design

A clear plan for every footprint.

The right layout depends on room width, openings, circulation, utilities and the number of people using the kitchen.

CORNER

L-Shaped

Open corners and efficient movement for compact or connected living spaces.

PARALLEL

Parallel / Galley

Two productive runs that keep storage, prep and cooking close.

THREE SIDES

U-Shaped

Generous work surface and storage across three connected sides.

CENTRAL

Island

A central zone for preparation, seating, storage or cooking.

LINEAR

One-Wall

A disciplined linear plan for studios, apartments and narrow rooms.

PENINSULA

G-Shaped / Peninsula

Extra counter space and zoning without a fully detached island.

Modular vs custom kitchen

Choose the build method that fits.

Both can deliver a refined kitchen. The difference is how the cabinets are engineered, fitted and installed.

SYSTEM

Modular kitchen

Pre-engineered modules support faster installation, consistent quality and efficient planning for standard layouts.

BESPOKE

Custom kitchen

Bespoke joinery is measured and made for a tailored fit, irregular spaces or very specific functional needs.

Our design process

Five practical steps.

Each stage is reviewed before the next begins, so the final kitchen is coordinated before installation.

01

Consultation & Requirements

We discuss cooking habits, storage, style, budget and timing.

02

Site Measurement

We record dimensions, utilities, openings and site constraints.

03

Concept & Layout Design

We test work zones, circulation and the cabinet arrangement.

04

Material & Furniture Selection

We select cabinetry finishes, counters, hardware and lighting.

05

Final Design Package & 3D Visualization

You receive coordinated drawings, selections and realistic views.

fields.heading: Kitchen design FAQs.
fields.copy: Straight answers to the questions we hear before a kitchen project begins.

items.q: What is the difference between modular and custom kitchens?
items.a: Modular kitchens use pre-engineered cabinet sizes and systems. Custom kitchens are measured and made for the exact room, layout and storage needs.

items.q: Which kitchen layout is best for my home?
items.a: It depends on room width, openings, utilities and daily use. We test L-shaped, U-shaped, galley, one-wall, peninsula and island options where suitable.

items.q: How long do design and installation take?
items.a: Design typically takes 1–2 weeks. Design plus installation typically takes 3–6 weeks, depending on whether the kitchen is modular or custom.

items.q: What is the kitchen work triangle?
items.a: It is the working relationship between the sink, stove and refrigerator. Good spacing between these points makes everyday cooking more efficient.

items.q: How do granite, marble and quartz compare?
items.a: Granite is durable and natural. Marble has a distinctive character but needs more care. Quartz is consistent, low-maintenance and available in many finishes.

items.q: Can you design a small kitchen?
items.a: Yes. Efficient layouts, full-height storage, pull-outs, corner solutions and integrated appliances make compact kitchens work harder.
